tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

content.content:
**Immutable releases:** The page has no dedicated config key for them. It appears only in the `preflight` block, added in **v2.18**, with `fail_on_error: true`. The comment says preflight can abort a release "when the token lacks permission to publish, or the current tag is already published as an immutable release that cannot be updated." A blog link titled "Moving to Immutable Releases" is listed under Updates, but its contents aren't included here.

**`draft`:** Set to `true` to avoid auto-publishing. The page says "all GitHub releases start as drafts while artifacts are uploaded." It also notes this is available only for GitHub and Gitea. No version is given.

**Publishing after upload:** The page doesn't describe this step directly. It can be inferred from the draft note above, which implies a release is published once uploads finish, unless `draft: true` is set.

**`replace_existing_artifacts: true`:** Removes an artifact already in the release, but only when an upload fails because it exists, which is a 422 on GitHub and a 400 on GitLab. It is available for GitHub and GitLab. No version is given.

A blog link titled "Moving to Immutable Releases" is listed under Updates, but its contents aren't included here.

**`draft`:** Set to `true` to avoid auto-publishing. The page says "all GitHub releases start as drafts while artifacts are uploaded." It also notes this is available only for GitHub and Gitea. No version is given.

**Publishing after upload:** The page doesn't describe this step directly. It can be inferred from the draft note above, which implies a release is published once uploads finish, unless `draft: true` is set.

**`replace_existing_draft: true`:** Applies "only if `draft` is set to true" and is GitHub-only, for removing existing drafts with the same name before creating a new one. No version is given.

**`use_existing_draft: true`:** Uses "an existing draft release as the target release." It is GitHub-only and was added in **v2.5**.

**`replace_existing_artifacts: true`:** Removes an artifact already in the release, but only when an upload fails because it exists, which is a 422 on GitHub and a 400 on GitLab. It is available for GitHub and GitLab. No version is given.

**Default SBOM config (from the page):**

- **`id`:** `default`
- **`artifacts`:** `archive`, which catalogs the archives produced by the archive step.
- **`documents`:** When `artifacts` is `archive` (the otherwise case), the default is `{{ .ArtifactName }}.sbom.json`. For `binary` it's `{{ .Binary }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}{{ targetVariant . }}.sbom.json`. For `any`, it's an empty list.
- **`cmd`:** `syft`
- **`args`:** `["$artifact", "--output", "spdx-json=$document", "--enrich", "all"]`. This produces SPDX JSON.

**CycloneDX:** The page doesn't give a default for CycloneDX. Its example uses `args: ["$artifact", "--output", "cyclonedx-json=$document"]`, which switches the output format.

**Checksums:** The page doesn't say whether SBOMs are included in checksums. You'd need the Checksums or SBOM reference pages to confirm that.

```yaml
checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt

signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    signature: "${artifact}.sigstore.json"
    args:
      - "sign-blob"
      - "--bundle=${signature}"
      - "${artifact}"
      - "--yes"
    artifacts: checksum
```

- **`cmd`**: `cosign`.
- **`args`**: `sign-blob`, then `--bundle=${signature}`, then `${artifact}`, then `--yes`. The `--yes` flag skips the interactive confirmation.

- **`artifacts: checksum`**: only the checksum file is signed.
- **`certificate`**: not set. The `--bundle` flag stores the certificate inside the `.sigstore.json` file, so no separate certificate template is needed.

content.content:
The page doesn't cover most of what you asked. It's a blog post announcing the policy, not a reference for the release mechanics.

**What the page does say:**

- **Policy:** GoReleaser now publishes releases that can't be changed later. As the post puts it, "no tag we publish can ever be overwritten."
- **Why the change was needed:** GitHub applies immutable releases to all releases at once, and GoReleaser used a moving `nightly` tag. Moving that tag would have conflicted with the setting.
- **Required changes:** They updated their action to v7.2.0 and "tune[d] our configuration a bit," but the post doesn't show that configuration.
- **Nightly tags:** Nightlies now use the format `{next-minor}-{sha}-nightly`, for example `v2.16.0-abc1234-nightly`. The old `nightly` tag remains but won't be updated and may be deleted.
- **Rationale:** Mutable tags let a compromised pipeline swap artifacts without users noticing. Immutable releases freeze each published version.

**Not covered in the page:**

- The order of draft creation, asset upload, and publishing
- Which version gets used for a release
- Preflight configuration
- `draft: true`, re-running a failed release, `use_existing_draft`, or attestations
- Any config snippets beyond the nightly tag format

The sidebar lists pages for GitHub release publishing (`customization/publish/scm/github/`) and attestations (`customization/publish/attestations/`). Those are the likely places to find the details, but I haven't seen their contents, so I can't summarize them here.

I can't quote the full page because of the 125-character limit on quotes, so here is a summary of the attestation details.

**What gets attested:** The page doesn't say GoReleaser creates attestations itself. It shows a release workflow that runs GitHub's attest action after GoReleaser finishes, on two outputs:
- `./dist/checksums.txt`, the release artifact checksums
- `./dist/digests.txt`, the Docker image digests (tag builds only)

**GoReleaser config keys:**
- `checksum.name_template`: set to `"checksums.txt"` so the filename is predictable.
- `docker_digest.name_template`: set to `"digests.txt"`.

**Required permissions:** The workflow needs `id-token: write` and `attestations: write`. The page notes that the second permission lets the workflow "write attestations."

**Immutable releases:** The page doesn't mention immutable releases.

**Recommended workflow:** The page doesn't use `actions/attest-build-provenance`. It uses `actions/attest@v4` with `subject-checksums`:
1. Run `goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v7`.
2. Run `actions/attest@v4` with `subject-checksums: ./dist/checksums.txt`.
3. Run `actions/attest@v4` with `subject-checksums: ./dist/digests.txt`, gated by `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`, since snapshots don't push Docker images.

**Verification:** Users can run `gh attestation verify --owner <user-or-org> <filename>` for files, or the same command with an image reference.

**Further reading:** The page links to an example repository (goreleaser/example-supply-chain) and to the checksum and Docker digest docs.

=== goreleaser/example-supply-chain/main/.goreleaser.yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
#
# Example keyless signing with SBOMs goreleaser config.
#
# See also: .github/workflows/release.yml
version: 2
project_name: supply-chain-example
# setups builds for linux and darwin on amd64 and arm64
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/build
builds:
  - env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    # ensures mod timestamp to be the commit timestamp
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
    flags:
      # trims path
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      # use commit date instead of current date as main.date
      # only needed if you actually use those things in your main package, otherwise can be ignored.
      - -s -w -X main.version={{.Version}} -X main.commit={{.Commit}} -X main.date={{ .CommitDate }}
# proxies from the go mod proxy before building
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/gomod
gomod:
  proxy: true
# config the checksum filename
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/checksum
checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"
# create a source tarball
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/source/
source:
  enabled: true
  name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}.src"
# config the archives filenames, format, and other options.
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/archive
archives:
  - formats: [tar.gz]
    wrap_in_directory: true
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    builds_info:
      mtime: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
# creates SBOMs of all archives and the source tarball using syft
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/sbom
sboms:
  - artifacts: archive
  - id: source # Two different sbom configurations need two different IDs
    artifacts: source
# signs the checksum file
# all files (including the sboms) are included in the checksum, so we don't need to sign each one if we don't want to
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/sign
signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    signature: "${artifact}.sigstore.json"
    args:
      - sign-blob
      - "--bundle=${signature}"
      - "${artifact}"
      - "--yes" # needed on cosign 2.0.0+
    artifacts: checksum
    output: true
# create a docker image
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/docker
dockers_v2:
  - images:
      - "ghcr.io/goreleaser/example-supply-chain"
    tags:
      - latest
      - "{{ .Tag }}"
    dockerfile: Dockerfile
    labels:
      org.opencontainers.image.created: "{{.Date}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.name: "{{.ProjectName}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.revision: "{{.FullCommit}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.version: "{{.Version}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.source: "{{.GitURL}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.description: "Example goreleaser + github actions config with keyless signing, SBOM generation, and attestations"
    annotations:
      "index:org.opencontainers.image.description": "Example goreleaser + github actions config with keyless signing, SBOM generation, and attestations"
# signs our docker image
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/docker_sign
docker_signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    output: true
    args:
      - "sign"
      - "${artifact}"
      - "--yes"

#
# Releaser workflow setup
# https://goreleaser.com/ci/actions/
#
name: release
# run only on tags
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
permissions:
  contents: write # needed to write releases
  id-token: write # needed for keyless signing
  packages: write # needed for ghcr access
  attestations: write # needed for provenance
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # this is important, otherwise it won't checkout the full tree (i.e. no previous tags)
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@99012661954931238ded8c8b007157a8430204e1 # v4.4.0
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action/download-syft@66cbf4bc1f1c0d2edc94016e65bc221b6bb0ad6c # v0.24.3
      - uses: docker/login-action@81c6f93d4bc991e510b342a00b419b3bb4efc5c6 # v4.7.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@a4f02ab5355a589de60d917a659ce617ed19b3de # v7.3.0
        with:
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-checksums: ./dist/checksums.txt
      - uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-checksums: ./dist/digests.txt

name: release
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "main"
    tags:
      - "v*"
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [goreleaser]
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    steps:
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
      - name: get tag
        run: echo "TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: download artifacts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release download "$TAG" \
            --repo goreleaser/goreleaser \
            --pattern 'goreleaser_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz' \
            --pattern 'checksums.txt' \
            --pattern 'checksums.txt.sigstore.json'
      - name: verify checksums
        run: shasum -a 256 --check --ignore-missing checksums.txt
      - name: verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify-blob \
            --certificate-identity "https://github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/$TAG" \
            --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' \
            --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
            checksums.txt
      - name: verify attestations
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh attestation verify goreleaser_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz \
            --repo goreleaser/goreleaser \
            --signer-repo goreleaser/goreleaser
  goreleaser-check-pkgs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      DOCKER_CLI_EXPERIMENTAL: "enabled"
    needs: [goreleaser]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    strategy:
      matrix:
        format: [deb, rpm, apk]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: go-task/setup-task@a00fbb05ce67b35648be3c78cbc9fd85354c757e # v2.2.0

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
#
# Example keyless signing with SBOMs goreleaser config.
#
# See also: .github/workflows/release.yml
version: 2
project_name: supply-chain-example
# setups builds for linux and darwin on amd64 and arm64
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/build
builds:
  - env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    # ensures mod timestamp to be the commit timestamp
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
    flags:
      # trims path
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      # use commit date instead of current date as main.date
      # only needed if you actually use those things in your main package, otherwise can be ignored.
      - -s -w -X main.version={{.Version}} -X main.commit={{.Commit}} -X main.date={{ .CommitDate }}
# proxies from the go mod proxy before building
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/gomod
gomod:
  proxy: true
# config the checksum filename
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/checksum
checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"
# create a source tarball
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/source/
source:
  enabled: true
  name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}.src"
# config the archives filenames, format, and other options.
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/archive
archives:
  - formats: [tar.gz]
    wrap_in_directory: true
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    builds_info:
      mtime: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
# creates SBOMs of all archives and the source tarball using syft
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/sbom
sboms:
  - artifacts: archive
  - id: source # Two different sbom configurations need two different IDs
    artifacts: source
# signs the checksum file
# all files (including the sboms) are included in the checksum, so we don't need to sign each one if we don't want to
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/sign
signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    signature: "${artifact}.sigstore.json"
    args:
      - sign-blob
      - "--bundle=${signature}"
      - "${artifact}"
      - "--yes" # needed on cosign 2.0.0+
    artifacts: checksum
    output: true
# create a docker image
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/docker
dockers_v2:
  - images:
      - "ghcr.io/goreleaser/example-supply-chain"
    tags:
      - latest
      - "{{ .Tag }}"
    dockerfile: Dockerfile
    labels:
      org.opencontainers.image.created: "{{.Date}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.name: "{{.ProjectName}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.revision: "{{.FullCommit}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.version: "{{.Version}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.source: "{{.GitURL}}"
      org.opencontainers.image.description: "Example goreleaser + github actions config with keyless signing, SBOM generation, and attestations"
    annotations:
      "index:org.opencontainers.image.description": "Example goreleaser + github actions config with keyless signing, SBOM generation, and attestations"
# signs our docker image
# https://goreleaser.com/customization/docker_sign
docker_signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    output: true
    args:
      - "sign"
      - "${artifact}"
      - "--yes"

name: 'Generate Generic Attestations'
description: 'Generate attestations for build artifacts'
author: 'GitHub'
branding:
  color: 'blue'
  icon: 'link'

inputs:
  subject-path:
    description: >
      Path to the artifact serving as the subject of the attestation. At most
      one of "subject-path", "subject-digest", or "subject-checksums" may be
      provided. May contain a glob pattern or list of paths (total subject
      count cannot exceed 1024). If none of these inputs are provided, subjects
      are discovered from the runner-provided $GITHUB_ARTIFACTS_LIST
      environment variable.
    required: false
  subject-digest:
    description: >
      Digest of the subject for the attestation. Must be in the form
      "algorithm:hex_digest" (e.g. "sha256:abc123..."). At most one of
      "subject-path", "subject-digest", or "subject-checksums" may be provided.
      If none are provided, subjects are discovered from
      $GITHUB_ARTIFACTS_LIST.
    required: false
  subject-name:
    description: >
      Subject name as it should appear in the attestation. Required when
      identifying the subject with the "subject-digest" input.
    required: false
  subject-checksums:
    description: >
      Path to checksums file containing digest and name of subjects for
      attestation. At most one of "subject-path", "subject-digest", or
      "subject-checksums" may be provided. If none are provided, subjects are
      discovered from $GITHUB_ARTIFACTS_LIST.
    required: false
  subject-version:
    description: >
      Version of the subject for the attestation. Only used when
      "push-to-registry" and "create-storage-record" are both set to true.
    required: false
  sbom-path:
    description: >
      Path to the JSON-formatted SBOM file (SPDX or CycloneDX) to attest.
      File size cannot exceed 16MB. When provided, creates an SBOM attestation.
      Cannot be used together with "predicate-type", "predicate", or
      "predicate-path".
    required: false
  predicate-type:
    description: >
      URI identifying the type of the predicate. Required when using "predicate"
      or "predicate-path" for custom attestations.
    required: false
  predicate:
    description: >
      String containing the value for the attestation predicate. String length
      cannot exceed 16MB. Must supply exactly one of "predicate-path" or
      "predicate" when creating custom attestations.
    required: false
  predicate-path:
    description: >
      Path to the file which contains the content for the attestation predicate.
      File size cannot exceed 16MB. Must supply exactly one of "predicate-path"
      or "predicate" when creating custom attestations.
    required: false
  push-to-registry:
    description: >
      Whether to push the attestation to the image registry. Requires that the
      resolved subject is a single fully-qualified OCI image reference with a
      SHA-256 digest, whether specified explicitly (via any subject input) or
      discovered from the runner-provided artifacts list. Defaults to false.
    default: false
    required: false
  create-storage-record:
    description: >
      Whether to create a storage record for the artifact.
      Requires that push-to-registry is set to true. Defaults to true.
    default: true
    required: false

content.content:
# entire-rsl

`entire rsl` shows what a repository's [gittuf](https://gittuf.dev) Reference
State Log (RSL) records for a branch, tag or Entire checkpoint: who pushed it,
when, and whether gittuf verification passes. It is a plugin for the
[Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) and also runs standalone as
`entire-rsl`.

entire-rsl is read-only, with exceptions that only touch gittuf refs:
`entire rsl refresh`, `--fetch`, and fetching a missing RSL when you agree to
it.

## Install

From a release, once published:

```sh
entire plugin install rsl
```

From a local build:

```sh
mise run build
entire plugin install ./bin/entire-rsl
```

## Quickstart

### 1. Create a repository on Entire

Follow the [Entire quickstart](https://docs.entire.com/quickstart) to install
the Entire CLI,
[create a repository on Entire](https://docs.entire.com/quickstart#create-a-new-repository-on-entire),
clone it and
[enable Entire](https://docs.entire.com/quickstart#2-open-a-repository-and-enable-entire)
in it. Then install entire-rsl (see [Install](#install)) and run the commands
below from the repository root.

### 2. Fetch the RSL

A new repository already has a policy and a first RSL entry. `refresh` fetches
them from `origin`, or from the remote you name:

```console
$ entire rsl refresh
Fetching gittuf refs from origin...
REF                              STATUS   LOCAL  REMOTE        COMMITS
refs/gittuf/policy               created  -      6cb81fc8b792  1 commit
refs/gittuf/reference-state-log  created  -      37d1fc96740f  1 commit (entry #1)
  `repositoryformatversion`, `filemode`, `bare`, `logallrefupdates`,
  `ignorecase`, `precomposeunicode`, `symlinks`; `extensions.objectformat`,
  `refstorage` and `worktreeconfig`; `remote.<name>` `url`, `pushurl`, `fetch`, `push`,
  `tagopt`, `mirror`, `prune`, `prunetags`, `promisor`,
  `partialclonefilter`, `entiredb-original-url`; every `branch.<name>` key,
  since git reads them only to pick upstreams and editors add their own;
  `user.name`, `email`, `signingkey`; `commit.gpgsign`, `tag.gpgsign`;
  `gpg.format`. The list was built from the `.git/config` of every
  repository under entireio. Any other key, or a listed key without the
  subsection its section needs, refuses the fetch with every offending key
  named once, sanitized, in git's order. Values are never shown. A failure
  to list the config is an error and nothing is fetched. There is no
  override: the user can fetch the gittuf refs with git.
- **Defence in depth:** the runner also passes `-c core.alternateRefsCommand=`,
  which a test shows makes git list an alternate's refs itself.
- **Per-worktree config:** `extensions.worktreeConfig` is allowed. It only
  makes git read `config.worktree`, whose keys are listed in the `worktree`
  scope and checked against the same allowlist.
- **Rejected:** extending the denylist, and an override flag.

## 2026-11-04: The fetch accepts only https:// and entire:// remote URLs

- **Context:** the fetch gate allowed `remote.<name>.url` with any value. A
  repository's own config could point the remote at a local path, `file://`,
  ssh or scp-like syntax, `git://`, plain `http://`, or another remote
  helper such as `fd::`. Entire's remotes are `https://`, or `entire://`
  through the Entire CLI's remote helper.
- **Decision:** before a fetch, every `remote.<name>.url` value in the
  `local` and `worktree` scopes must start with `https://` or `entire://`,
  for every remote, not only the one fetched. The prefix matches
  case-sensitively, as git picks a transport or remote helper by the scheme
  as written. A key without a value is refused. The key is named with
  `(not an https:// or entire:// URL)`, and the URL is never shown, since
  it can hold credentials. `pushurl` is not checked, as a fetch never uses
  it. A rewrite through `url.<base>.insteadOf` is still refused in the
  repository's config and trusted in global config, like every other key.
- **Tests:** fixtures clone from `https://local.test/<path>`, which the
  global config `testutil.IsolateGitConfig` writes rewrites to `file:///`.
- **Rejected:** a case-insensitive match, and checking only the fetched
  remote.

            echo "could not read the golangci-lint version from mise.toml" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=v$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

input.content:
name: Release
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      # Create the draft release and upload its assets.
      contents: write
      # Mint the OIDC token behind the keyless cosign signature and the
      # provenance attestation.
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # goreleaser reads the previous tag from history.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Installs goreleaser, cosign and syft at the versions in mise.toml.
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4

      # Uploads archives, SBOMs, checksums.txt and its Sigstore bundle to a
      # draft release. See the release section of .goreleaser.yaml.
      - name: Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: goreleaser release --clean

      # Stored by GitHub's attestation API, not as a release asset, so it
      # works on a draft and needs no change to the release.
      - name: Attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-checksums: ./dist/checksums.txt

      # Checks what users will check, before a maintainer publishes the
      # draft and makes it immutable.
      - name: Verify signature, checksums and provenance
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          WORKFLOW_REF: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}
        working-directory: dist
        run: |
          cosign verify-blob \
            --certificate-identity "https://github.com/${WORKFLOW_REF}" \
            --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
            --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
            checksums.txt
          sha256sum --check --strict checksums.txt
          for f in *.tar.gz *.zip; do
            gh attestation verify "$f" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --signer-workflow "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/.github/workflows/release.yml"
          done

name: Release
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      # Create the draft release and upload its assets.
      contents: write
      # Mint the OIDC token behind the keyless cosign signature and the
      # provenance attestation.
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # goreleaser reads the previous tag from history.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Installs goreleaser, cosign and syft at the versions in mise.toml.
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4

      # Uploads archives, SBOMs, checksums.txt and its Sigstore bundle to a
      # draft release. See the release section of .goreleaser.yaml.
      - name: Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: goreleaser release --clean

      # Stored by GitHub's attestation API, not as a release asset, so it
      # works on a draft and needs no change to the release.
      - name: Attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-checksums: ./dist/checksums.txt

      # Checks what users will check, before a maintainer publishes the
      # draft and makes it immutable.
      - name: Verify signature, checksums and provenance
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          WORKFLOW_REF: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}
        working-directory: dist
        run: |
          cosign verify-blob \
            --certificate-identity "https://github.com/${WORKFLOW_REF}" \
            --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
            --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
            checksums.txt
          sha256sum --check --strict checksums.txt
          for f in *.tar.gz *.zip; do
            gh attestation verify "$f" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --signer-workflow "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/.github/workflows/release.yml"
          done

cd ~/git/entireio/entire-rsl && cat >> docs/decisions.md <<'EOF'

## 2026-11-04: Signed releases with SBOMs, safe under immutable releases

- **Context:** releases shipped archives and `checksums.txt` only, with no
  release workflow. The repository may enable GitHub immutable releases,
  which freeze a release's assets and tag once it is published, so nothing
  can be added after publishing and a published tag cannot be released
  again.
- **Decision:** `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs goreleaser on a `v*`
  tag. syft writes one SPDX JSON SBOM per archive, before the checksum step,
  so `checksums.txt` covers them. cosign signs `checksums.txt` keyless with
  the workflow's OIDC identity into `checksums.txt.sigstore.json`.
  `actions/attest` records build provenance for every file in
  `checksums.txt`. The job then verifies the signature, the checksums and
  the provenance. goreleaser uploads everything to a draft that a
  maintainer publishes, so every asset is in place before the release
  becomes immutable. Attestations live in GitHub's attestation API, not in
  the release. `replace_existing_draft` keeps a re-run from leaving a second
  draft, and `preflight.fail_on_error` stops a run for a tag that already
  has an immutable release. cosign and syft are pinned in `mise.toml`.
  `mise run snapshot` skips signing, which needs the CI identity.
- **Consequences:** a published release cannot be fixed. A broken one needs a
  new tag. Signing records the repository, workflow and tag in the public
  Rekor log. Attestations in a private repository need GitHub Enterprise
  Cloud.
- **Rejected:** signing each archive (the signed checksums cover them),
  CycloneDX (SPDX is goreleaser's default and what GitHub's dependency graph
  exports), uploading signatures after goreleaser publishes (refused once
  the release is immutable), and the mise-action cache in the release job
  (zizmor `cache-poisoning`).
EOF
export MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS=$PWD; git diff --stat; mise run check 2>&1 | tail -8

content.text:
I've added a tag-triggered release workflow (the repo didn't have one) with Sigstore signing, SPDX SBOMs and build provenance, set up so it works with immutable releases. The signing, attestation and draft upload only run on GitHub, so they haven't run yet. The first `v*` tag push will be their first real test.

**What a release now produces** (`.goreleaser.yaml`, new `.github/workflows/release.yml`)
- **SBOMs:** one SPDX JSON SBOM per archive (`<archive>.sbom.json`), generated by syft. A local snapshot produced SPDX 2.3 files listing 180 packages, gittuf and go-git included.
- **Signature:** cosign signs `checksums.txt` keyless, as the workflow identity, into `checksums.txt.sigstore.json`. The SBOMs are generated before the checksums, so `checksums.txt` lists them too and one signature covers archives and SBOMs.
- **Provenance:** `actions/attest` (v4.2.2, pinned by SHA) records build provenance for every file listed in `checksums.txt`.
- **Self-check:** the job then verifies the cosign bundle against the exact workflow identity, the checksums, and the provenance for each archive. It does this before anyone publishes.

**Immutable releases**
- GoReleaser 2.18.3 creates the release as a draft and uploads everything before publishing; I checked this in its source. `draft: true` is kept, so a maintainer publishes after the job passes. Nothing is added to the release after that.
- The provenance is stored in GitHub's attestation API, not as a release asset, so it never needs to change the release.
- `replace_existing_draft: true`: re-running a failed job replaces the old draft instead of leaving two.
- `preflight.fail_on_error: true`: a tag that already has a published immutable release is rejected before anything is built.

**Supporting changes**
- `mise.toml` pins `cosign` 3.1.4 and `syft` 1.56.0, so CI and local runs use the same tools. Every CI job now installs both.
- `mise run snapshot` now skips signing, because keyless signing only works with the CI identity.
- The release job turns off the mise-action cache, so it can't pick up a cache written by another run (a zizmor finding).
- `README.md` explains how users verify a download, and `docs/decisions.md` records the decision.

**Checks:** `goreleaser check`, a local snapshot, actionlint, zizmor (no findings) and `mise run check` all pass.

**Before the first release**
- While the repo is private, provenance attestations need GitHub Enterprise Cloud. Without it the attest step fails after the draft is uploaded. The draft stays a draft, but you'd need to make the repo public first or remove the step.
- Signing writes the repo name, workflow path and tag to the public Rekor transparency log.
- With immutable releases on, a broken published release can't be fixed. The only way out is a new tag.

Nothing is committed yet. On `workflows`, the planned commit is:

```

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
```

It covers `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.goreleaser.yaml`, `mise.toml`, `README.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. The commit is signed, so it will ask for a security-key touch. Shall I commit?
